title: Molecular Spring Constant Analysis by Biomembrane Force Probe Spectroscopy
protocol: Start the experiment in the software for BFP control and parameter setting.
Observe repetitive probe bead-target bead/cell touches in the software for BFP Monitor.
Tune impingement force and contact time to achieve an adhesion frequency ≤ 20% within the first 50 touches.
Save data, in the form of Force vs. Time, to a user-directed folder at the end of each pair.
Collect raw data of bond events using the BFP acquisition platform.
Open the BFP data analysis software and select corresponding raw data file by double clicking on them.
Run the program and switch between events using up and down buttons.
Screen out invalid events using outlier exclusion criteria.
Select exporting data type as Force vs. Time format and click on Export Plots Data button.
Convert the force vs. time curve to a force vs. displacement curve.
Export the data segment corresponding to the Retract stage to a spreadsheet.
Plot the Force vs. Time Curve using spreadsheet software.
Convert time values to total displacement values by multiplying with piezo movement velocity (4,000 nm/s).
Zero the first data point by subtracting the smallest displacement value from each acquired displacement value.
Plot the Force vs. Displacement curve as shown in Figure 2B.
Fit a regression line to each data group in the Force vs. Displacement curve for compressive and tensile phases.
Express the reciprocal of the total spring constant (ktot) as the sum of the spring constant inverses of RBC, molecular bond, and target cell during the compressive phase.
Exclude the molecular bond contribution (kmol) when calculating ktot during the compressive phase.
Use equation 3 to calculate kRBC with acquired k1 and predetermined kRBC value.
Calculate kcell from equation 3 using the acquired k1 and predetermined kRBC value.
Express the reciprocal of the total spring constant as the sum of RBC, molecular bond, and target cell during the tensile phase.
Include adhesion formation between ligand-receptor pair in calculations for the tensile phase.
Use equation 4 to calculate ktot (k2) during the tensile phase.
Derive kmol by subtracting 1/k1 from 1/k2.
Fit a regression line to the compressive phase data to obtain k1.
Fit a regression line to the tensile phase data to obtain k2.
Derive kmol by subtracting 1/k1 from 1/k2.
